draft.title: Significant figures
card: Significant figures are the digits that carry the size of a number. Counting starts at the first non-zero digit and moves right.
Zeros before the first non-zero digit only show place value, so they are not counted. Zeros between non-zero digits are counted, so 2.07 has 3 significant figures.
To round, keep the number of digits asked for. Look at the next digit. If it is 5 or more, round the last kept digit up. If it is 4 or less, leave it.
Worked example: round 0.004 562 to 2 significant figures. The first two are 4 and 5, and the next digit is 6, so the 5 becomes 6. The answer is 0.0046.
draft.remember: Skip the zeros at the start, count the zeros in between, then round using the next digit.

a.q: Round 0.007 381 to 2 significant figures. What is the answer?
a.why: The first significant figure is 7, so the two digits are 7 and 3. The next digit is 8, so the 3 rounds up to 4, giving 0.0074. Rounding down to 0.0073 ignores the 8.
a.clue: Start counting at the first digit that is not zero.

b.q: A rock pool at Bondi holds 0.030 468 megalitres of water. What is this to 3 significant figures?
b.why: Counting starts at the 3, and the zero between 3 and 4 is counted, so the three digits are 3, 0 and 4. The next digit is 6, so the 4 rounds up to 5, giving 0.0305. 0.0304 forgets to round up.
b.clue: Does the zero after the 3 count as a significant figure?
